title.en: Volume 293 Biographies 80: Li Fu, Cai Ting, Xie Jishi, Chen Xuehai
title.raw: 卷293 列傳八十 李绂 蔡珽 谢济世 陈学海

sentences.zh: 列傳八十

translations.literal: Biography 80
translations.idiomatic: Biography 80

sentences.zh: 李紱蔡珽謝濟世陳學海

translations.literal: Li Fu, Cai Ting, Xie Jishi, and Chen Xuehai
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, Cai Ting, Xie Jishi, and Chen Xuehai

sentences.zh: 李紱，字巨來，江西臨川人。

translations.literal: Li Fu, styled Julai, was a native of Linchuan in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, whose style was Julai, came from Linchuan in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，好學，讀書經目成誦。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he loved learning; after reading a text once he could recite it from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Left fatherless while still young and in poverty, he devoted himself to study and could recite a passage after a single reading.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年，成進士，改庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi examination, was made a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy, and after completing his palace studies was appointed revising editor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 48 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and on completing his academy term received appointment as a revising editor.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to the post of Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，擢內閣學士，尋遷左副都御史，仍兼學士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was elevated to Grand Secretariat academician, and soon after transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief while retaining his academician status.
translations.idiomatic: In year 59 he was promoted to Grand Secretariat academician and shortly thereafter moved to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, still holding his academician title.

sentences.zh: 六十年，充會試副考官。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 60 he served as deputy examiner for the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 出榜日，黃霧風霾，上語大學士等曰：「此榜或有亂臣賊子，否亦當有讀書積學之士不得中式，怨氣所致。

translations.literal: On the day the list was published, yellow fog and wind-blown haze prevailed; the emperor said to the grand secretaries and others: "This list may contain traitorous ministers and wicked sons, or else men of deep learning who failed to pass through resentment—that is what has caused this."
translations.idiomatic: When the examination results were posted, yellow haze and windblown dust filled the air. The emperor told the grand secretaries and his colleagues, "This cohort may hold traitors and scoundrels—or else learned scholars who were shut out of the degrees, and their resentment has brought this on."

sentences.zh: 」命磨勘試卷，劣者停殿試。

translations.literal: " He ordered the examination papers reviewed again, and the inferior were barred from the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the papers re-examined and disqualified the poorest candidates from the palace test.

sentences.zh: 又賜滿洲舉人留保、直隸舉人王蘭生進士。

translations.literal: He also granted jinshi status to the Manchu licentiate Liubao and the Zhili licentiate Wang Lansheng.
translations.idiomatic: He further conferred jinshi degrees on the Manchu provincial graduate Liubao and the Zhili graduate Wang Lansheng.

sentences.zh: 下第舉子群聚紱門，投瓦石喧閧。

translations.literal: Failed candidates gathered at Fu's gate in a mob, throwing tiles and stones in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who had failed clustered at Fu's gate, hurling tiles and stones amid an uproar.

sentences.zh: 御史舒庫疏劾，下部議，責紱匿不奏，奪官，發永定河工效力。

translations.literal: Censor Shu Ku memorialized in impeachment; the matter was referred to the ministries for deliberation; Fu was charged with concealing the incident and failing to report it, stripped of office, and sent to labor at the Yongding River works.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shu Ku impeached him. After ministry review Fu was found to have suppressed the riot without reporting it, deprived of his post, and sent to serve at the Yongding River project.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，特命复官，署吏部侍郎，赴山東催漕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was specially ordered restored to office, acting Vice Minister of Personnel, and sent to Shandong to hasten the grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he was specially reinstated as acting Vice Minister of Personnel and dispatched to Shandong to press the grain transport.

sentences.zh: 尋授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 上令截留湖南等省漕糧於天津收貯，旋又命估價出糶。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the transport grain from Hunan and other provinces held at Tianjin for storage, and soon afterward ordered it sold at appraised price.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor directed that transport grain from Hunan and other provinces be stored at Tianjin, then soon ordered it sold off at market appraisal.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，授廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year he was appointed Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 2 he was made Governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「廣西賀縣大金、蕉木二山產礦砂，五十里外為廣東梅峒汛，又數里為宿塘寨，礦徒盤據，時時竊發。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "In He County of Guangxi, Mt. Dajin and Mt. Jiaomu produce ore; fifty li beyond lies the Meidong garrison of Guangdong, and a few li farther is Sutang Stockade; miners occupy the area and frequently raid in secret."
translations.idiomatic: He reported: "At Dajin and Jiaomu mountains in He County, Guangxi, ore is mined. Fifty li away stands Guangdong's Meidong garrison; a few li beyond that lies Sutang Stockade. Miners hold these sites and raid the countryside from time to time."

sentences.zh: 臣方擬嚴禁，聞總督孔毓珣條陳開採，因而中止。

translations.literal: "Your servant was about to impose strict prohibition when he heard that Governor-General Kong Yuqin had memorialized proposing to open mining, and therefore suspended action."
translations.idiomatic: "I was preparing a strict ban when word came that Governor-General Kong Yuqin had submitted plans to open the mines, so I halted enforcement."

sentences.zh: 將來或恐滋事。

translations.literal: "In future trouble may arise."
translations.idiomatic: "Violence may yet follow."

sentences.zh: 」毓珣奏同時至，廷議寢其事。

translations.literal: " Kong Yuqin's memorial arrived at the same time, and court deliberation shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuqin's own memorial arrived simultaneously, and the court set the proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 上命以諭毓珣者示紱，令協力禁止。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered that what had been told Yuqin be shown to Fu and that they cooperate in prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Fu the instructions given Yuqin and told both men to work together to suppress mining.

sentences.zh: 紱疏陳練兵，列舉嚴賞罰、演陣法、習用槍砲、豫備帳房鑼鍋諸事，上嘉其留心武備。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized on troop training, listing strict rewards and punishments, drilling battle formations, practicing with guns and cannon, and preparing tents, gongs, and camp kettles; the emperor praised his attention to military readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Fu submitted a plan for drilling troops, detailing strict rewards and punishments, formation practice, musket and artillery drill, and the provisioning of tents, gongs, and camp kettles. The throne commended his care for military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，巡撫陳元龍奏請開捐，都計收穀百十七萬石有奇，石折銀一兩一錢，而發州縣買穀石止三錢，不足以糴。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period Governor Chen Yuanlong memorialized to open contribution sales; in all more than 1,170,000 shi of grain was collected, each shi converted at 1 tael 1 qian of silver, yet the grain released to prefectures and counties for purchase was priced at only 3 qian per shi—not enough to buy grain.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi, Governor Chen Yuanlong had opened the sale of offices for grain contributions. The treasury took in more than 1,170,000 shi, reckoned at 1.1 taels of silver per shi, yet when the prefectures and counties went to purchase grain the price set was only 3 cash per shi—far too little to fill the quotas.

sentences.zh: 至紱上官，尚虧四萬餘石，紱奏請限一月補足。

translations.literal: By the time Fu took office more than 40,000 shi were still in deficit; Fu memorialized asking for one month to make it good.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu arrived there was still a shortfall of over forty thousand shi; he asked for one month to restore the full amount.

sentences.zh: 會提督韓良輔條奏墾荒，下紱議，紱請以桂林、柳州、梧州、南寧四府收貯捐穀動支為開墾費。

translations.literal: At the same time Regional Commander Han Liangfu memorialized on reclaiming wasteland; the matter was sent to Fu for deliberation, and Fu asked that grain from contribution stores in the four prefectures Guilin, Liuzhou, Wuzhou, and Nanning be drawn for reclamation expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Han Liangfu meanwhile submitted plans for opening wasteland. The matter went to Fu for review; Fu proposed spending contribution grain held in Guilin, Liuzhou, Wuzhou, and Nanning.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕觀紱意，不過借開墾以銷捐穀。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I see Fu's intent is nothing but to use reclamation to write off contribution grain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Fu's scheme is simply to clear the contribution shortfall under the cover of land reclamation."

sentences.zh: 當時陳元龍等首尾不清，朕知之甚詳。

translations.literal: "At that time Chen Yuanlong and the like were inconsistent from start to finish; I know this in very great detail."
translations.idiomatic: "Chen Yuanlong's accounts were a tangle from first to last—I know every thread of it."

sentences.zh: 應令元龍等往廣西料理。

translations.literal: "Yuanlong and the others ought to be sent to Guangxi to settle the matter."
translations.idiomatic: "Yuanlong and his associates should go to Guangxi and put the books in order."

sentences.zh: 」並諭紱詳察，毋隱諱瞻徇，自承虧空。

translations.literal: " He also instructed Fu to investigate thoroughly, not conceal or show partiality, or bear the deficit himself.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor also warned Fu to investigate without concealment, favoritism, or shouldering the loss himself.

sentences.zh: 尋紱奏察出督撫、司道、府廳分得羨餘銀八十二萬有奇，勒限分償，上嘉紱秉公執正。

translations.literal: Soon Fu memorialized that he had found governors, provincial commissioners, prefects, and subprefects had split surplus silver totaling more than 820,000 taels, and ordered them to repay within a deadline; the emperor praised Fu for upholding justice impartially.
translations.idiomatic: Fu soon reported that provincial officials had divided more than 820,000 taels in surpluses among themselves and ordered repayment on a fixed schedule. The throne praised his impartiality.

sentences.zh: 紱在吏部時，年羹堯子富等捐造營房，下部議敘，不肯從優，為羹堯所嫉；

translations.literal: While Fu was at the Ministry of Personnel, the sons of Nian Gengyao—Fu and others—made contribution donations to build barracks; when referred to the ministries for commendation Fu would not grant preferential treatment and was hated by Gengyao;
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry of Personnel, Gengyao's sons and others had donated funds to erect barracks. When the ministry considered reward for the gift, Fu refused preferential treatment, and Gengyao came to resent him;

sentences.zh: 及上命天津截漕估糶盈餘銀五千交守道桑成鼎貯庫，紱至廣西，成鼎使齎以畀紱。

translations.literal: when the emperor ordered the surplus of 5,000 taels from holding and selling grain at Tianjin turned over to Surveillance Commissioner Sang Chengdian for the treasury, Fu went to Guangxi, and Chengdian had someone deliver it to Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor ordered five thousand taels of surplus silver from the Tianjin grain operation placed with Surveillance Commissioner Sang Chengdian. When Fu reached Guangxi, Chengdian sent the sum to him.

sentences.zh: 紱具摺送直隸巡撫李維鈞會奏。

translations.literal: Fu prepared a memorial and sent it to Zhili Governor Li Weijun for joint submission.
translations.idiomatic: Fu drew up a memorial and sent it to Zhili Governor Li Weijun for joint presentation.

sentences.zh: 維鈞匿不上，紱乃奏聞。

translations.literal: Weijun concealed it and did not submit; Fu then memorialized directly.
translations.idiomatic: Weijun withheld it, so Fu reported directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 先是，羹堯朝京師，入對，舉此訐紱，謂紱乾沒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gengyao came to the capital for audience he cited this to denounce Fu, saying Fu had embezzled the funds.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gengyao, on arriving at court, had denounced Fu on this ground, claiming embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 上以問維鈞，維鈞言紱取數百金治裝，餘尚貯庫。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Weijun; Weijun said Fu had taken several hundred taels for travel expenses and the rest remained in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Weijun, who said Fu had taken a few hundred taels for traveling expenses while the remainder stayed in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 紱奏至，上謂維鈞與羹堯比，欲陷紱。

translations.literal: When Fu's memorial arrived the emperor said Weijun was in league with Gengyao to entrap Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's memorial arrived, and the emperor concluded Weijun was conspiring with Gengyao to frame him.

sentences.zh: 諭獎紱，命留充公用。

translations.literal: He issued commendation to Fu and ordered the sum retained for public use.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Fu and directed that the silver be kept for public purposes.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，紱奏言：「太平、思恩府界流言安南內亂。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year Fu memorialized: "On the border between Taiping and Si'en prefectures rumors tell of internal disorder in Annam."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year three Fu reported: "Along the Taiping–Si'en border word spreads of civil strife in Annam."

sentences.zh: 有潘騰龍者，自言為莫姓後，其黨黃把勢、陳亂彈等煽誘為亂。

translations.literal: "One Pan Tenglong claims to be of the Mo clan; his followers Huang Bashitou, Chen Luandan, and others incite sedition."
translations.idiomatic: "A man named Pan Tenglong claims descent from the Mo royal house; his followers Huang Bashitou and Chen Luandan urge rebellion."

sentences.zh: 嚴飭將吏捕治。

translations.literal: "I have strictly ordered military and civil officers to arrest and punish them."
translations.idiomatic: "I have ordered officers to arrest and punish them without delay."

sentences.zh: 」上諭曰：「封疆之內，宜整理振作。

translations.literal: " The emperor instructed: "Within the borders one should put affairs in order and rouse one's spirit."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "Within your jurisdiction you must set affairs in order and rouse the administration."

sentences.zh: 至於安邊柔遠，最忌貪利圖功，當慎之又慎！

translations.literal: "As for pacifying the frontier and soothing distant peoples, one must above all beware of greed for profit and schemes for merit—be exceedingly cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: "Pacifying borders and winning distant peoples demands the utmost caution against greed and vainglory—be doubly wary!"

sentences.zh: 」九月，奏：「瑤、僮頑梗，修仁十排、天河三甿為尤甚，常出劫掠。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month he memorialized: "The Yao and Zhuang are obstinate; the Ten Pai of Xiuren and the Sanmu of Tianhe are worst, constantly raiding."
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month he reported: "The Yao and Zhuang remain defiant—the Ten Rows of Xiuren and the Three Villages of Tianhe worst of all—plundering constantly."

sentences.zh: 臣遣吏入十排，捕得其渠。

translations.literal: "Your servant sent clerks into the Ten Pai and captured their ringleader."
translations.idiomatic: "I sent officials into the Ten Rows and seized the chief."

sentences.zh: 三甿阻萬山中，所種田在隘外。

translations.literal: "Sanmu lies behind precipitous mountains; their fields lie outside the passes."
translations.idiomatic: "The Three Villages lie deep in the mountains; their crops stand beyond the passes."

sentences.zh: 臣發兵守隘，斷其收穫。

translations.literal: "Your servant sent troops to hold the passes and cut off their harvest."
translations.idiomatic: "I posted troops at the passes to deny them the harvest."

sentences.zh: 其渠今亦出自歸。

translations.literal: "Their ringleader has now come forth to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: "Their leader has now surrendered of his own accord."

sentences.zh: 」上獎其辦理得宜。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised his handling as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised his handling of the matter.

sentences.zh: 旋授直隸總督。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Governor-General of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 四年，紱入覲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Fu came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Fu came to court for audience.

sentences.zh: 初，左都御史蔡珽薦起其故吏知縣黃振國授河南信陽知州，忤巡撫田文鏡。

translations.literal: Earlier, Left Censor-in-Chief Cai Ting had recommended his former subordinate Magistrate Huang Zhenguo for appointment as prefect of Xinyang in Henan, offending Governor Tian Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Left Censor-in-Chief Cai Ting had revived his former subordinate Magistrate Huang Zhenguo and secured his appointment as prefect of Xinyang, Henan—a move that angered Governor Tian Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 文鏡馭吏嚴，尤惡科目，劾振國貪劣。

translations.literal: Wenjing governed subordinates strictly and especially hated examination graduates; he impeached Zhenguo for greed and misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing ran his staff with an iron hand and especially despised men who came up through the examinations; he impeached Zhenguo for corruption and baseness.

sentences.zh: 紱過河南，詰文鏡胡為有意蹂踐士人。

translations.literal: Passing through Henan, he interrogated Wenjing as to why he deliberately trampled on scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Henan, he challenged Wenjing for deliberately humiliating the degree-holding class.

sentences.zh: 入對，因極言文鏡貪虐，且謂文鏡所劾屬吏，如振國及邵言綸、汪諴皆枉，振國已死獄中。

translations.literal: At audience he spoke at length of Wenjing's greed and cruelty, and said subordinates Wenjing had impeached, such as Zhenguo as well as Shao Yanlun and Wang Shen, were all wronged; Zhenguo had already died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he spoke at length against Wenjing's greed and cruelty, saying the men Wenjing had impeached—including Zhenguo, Shao Yanlun, and Wang Shen—were innocent, and that Zhenguo had already died in prison.

sentences.zh: 文鏡因紱語，先密疏聞，謂紱與振國同年袒護。

translations.literal: Wenjing, because of Fu's words, first sent a secret memorial reporting that Fu and Zhenguo were of the same year and shielding each other.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Fu's remarks Wenjing filed a secret memorial first, alleging that Fu and Zhenguo, having passed the exams in the same year, were covering for each other.

sentences.zh: 紱疏辨，上不直紱，而振國實未死，逮至京師，上更謂紱妄語。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized in defense; the emperor did not favor Fu, yet Zhenguo had not in fact died and was brought to the capital; the emperor further said Fu had spoken falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized in his own defense, but the emperor sided against him. Zhenguo was still alive and was brought to the capital, so the emperor charged Fu with false testimony.

sentences.zh: 良輔奏雲南、廣西所屬土司與貴州接壤者，皆改歸貴州安籠鎮節制，命紱往與雲貴總督高其倬會勘，疏請循舊制，從之。

translations.literal: Liangfu memorialized that native chieftains under Yunnan and Guangxi bordering Guizhou should all come under the control of Anlong Garrison in Guizhou; the emperor ordered Fu to join Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Gao Qishen in surveying; Fu memorialized asking to follow the old system, and it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Liangfu proposed placing all Yunnan and Guangxi native offices bordering Guizhou under Anlong Garrison. Fu was sent to survey with Governor-General Gao Qishen; Fu asked to keep the old arrangement, and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 紱還直隸，時上譴責諸弟允禩、允禟等，更允禟名塞思黑，幽諸西寧，复移置保定，命胡什禮監送。

translations.literal: Fu returned to Zhili; at the time the emperor was reprimanding his brothers Yinqi and Yinzi, renamed Yinzi Seshei, confined him at Xining, then moved him to Baoding, and ordered Hu Shili to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Zhili, Fu found the emperor rebuking his brothers Yinqi and Yinzi. Yinzi was renamed Seshei, imprisoned at Xining, then moved to Baoding under escort by Hu Shili.

sentences.zh: 紱語胡什禮：「塞思黑至，當便宜行事。

translations.literal: Fu told Hu Shili: "When Seshei arrives, act as circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: Fu told Hu Shili, "When Seshei arrives, deal with him as the situation demands."

sentences.zh: 」胡什禮以聞，上以為不可，命諭紱，紱奏初無此語。

translations.literal: " Hu Shili reported this; the emperor thought it unacceptable and ordered Fu informed; Fu memorialized that he had never said this.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu Shili reported the remark. The emperor rejected it and sent instructions to Fu, who memorialized that he had never spoken such words.

sentences.zh: 塞思黑至保定，未幾，紱以病聞，尋遂死。

translations.literal: Seshei reached Baoding; before long Fu reported illness, and soon Seshei died.
translations.idiomatic: Seshei reached Baoding. Before long Fu reported that Seshei was ill, and soon Seshei died.

sentences.zh: 是冬，御史謝濟世劾文鏡貪虐，仍及誣劾振國等。

translations.literal: That winter Censor Xie Jishi impeached Wenjing for greed and cruelty, again touching on the false impeachment of Zhenguo and others.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Censor Xie Jishi impeached Wenjing again for greed and cruelty, including the false charges against Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 上奪濟世官，下大學士九卿會鞫，戍濟世阿爾泰軍前。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Jishi of office, referred the matter to the grand secretaries and Nine Ministers for joint trial, and banished Jishi to the Altai front.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deprived Jishi of his post, convened the grand secretaries and Nine Ministers, and banished him to service before the Altai armies.

sentences.zh: 上以濟世奏與紱語同，疑紱與為黨，召紱授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Because Jishi's memorial matched Fu's words the emperor suspected Fu was his partisan and summoned Fu to appoint him Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi's memorial echoed Fu's language, so the emperor suspected conspiracy and summoned Fu to make him Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 紱在廣西捕亂苗莫東旺置天河縣獄，獄未竟，紱移督直隸去。

translations.literal: Fu in Guangxi had captured the rebellious Miao Mo Dongwang and placed him in Tianhe county prison; the case was unfinished when Fu left as Zhili governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi Fu had arrested the rebel Miao Mo Dongwang and jailed him at Tianhe, but the case was unfinished when he left for Zhili.

sentences.zh: 久之，蠻、僮集眾破獄，劫東旺去。

translations.literal: After a long time the Miao and Zhuang gathered in a mob, broke the prison, and carried Dongwang off.
translations.idiomatic: Later the tribesmen stormed the prison and freed Dongwang.

sentences.zh: 五年春，良輔署廣西巡撫，奏聞。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year Liangfu, acting as Guangxi governor, memorialized report.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year five Liangfu, acting governor, reported the breakout.

sentences.zh: 上以詰紱，下部察議。

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated Fu and referred the matter to the ministries for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Fu and sent the matter for ministry review.

sentences.zh: 會都察院奏廣西州判程旦詣院訴土司羅文剛掠村落抗官兵，上責紱與繼任巡撫甘汝來逡巡貽害，命紱與汝來至廣西捕治，不獲，當重譴。

translations.literal: At the same time the Censorate memorialized that Guangxi subprefectural judge Cheng Dan had come to the court complaining that native chieftain Luo Wengang had raided villages and resisted government troops; the emperor blamed Fu and his successor Governor Gan Rulai for dilatory conduct that invited harm, ordered Fu and Rulai to Guangxi to capture and punish him, and on failure they would face severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate reported that Judge Cheng Dan had petitioned the court: native chieftain Luo Wengang was raiding villages and fighting troops. The emperor blamed Fu and successor Gan Rulai for delay that let harm spread, and ordered both to Guangxi to capture Wengang—on failure they would be heavily punished.

sentences.zh: 紱至廣西，東旺聞而自歸，文剛亦捕得。

translations.literal: Fu reached Guangxi; Dongwang heard and surrendered himself; Wengang was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: Fu reached Guangxi; Dongwang surrendered on hearing of his arrival, and Wengang was seized.

sentences.zh: 直隸總督宜兆熊劾知府曾逢聖、知縣王遊虧空錢糧，上以逢聖、遊皆紱所薦，命詰紱。

translations.literal: Zhili Governor Yizhaoxiong impeached prefect Zeng Fengsheng and magistrate Wang You for deficits in tax grain; because Fengsheng and You were both recommended by Fu, the emperor ordered Fu questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yizhaoxiong impeached Prefect Zeng Fengsheng and Magistrate Wang You for grain deficits. Both had been Fu's appointees, so the emperor summoned Fu to account.

sentences.zh: 戶部議覆，紱在直隸奏報懷來倉圮，穀為小民竊食，當下直隸總督詳察。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated and replied: Fu in Zhili had reported the Huailai granary collapsed and commoners stole the grain; Zhili governor should be ordered to investigate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue deliberation noted that Fu had reported the Huailai granary wall collapsed and that villagers stole grain; the Zhili governor should investigate.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「穀至六千餘石，豈能竊食至盡？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Grain amounted to more than 6,000 shi—how could stealing by commoners consume it all?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "More than six thousand shi were stored—could villagers really eat it all?"

sentences.zh: 明系紱市恩，為縣吏脫罪。

translations.literal: "Clearly Fu was currying favor, securing exemption for county officials."
translations.idiomatic: "Fu was plainly currying favor to shield county clerks."

sentences.zh: 當責紱償補，以成其市恩。

translations.literal: "Fu should be ordered to make repayment, thereby completing his currying of favor."
translations.idiomatic: "Make Fu pay restitution—that will complete his favor-buying."

sentences.zh: 」兆熊又劾知縣李先枝私派累民，上以先枝亦紱所薦，責紱欺罔，奪官；

translations.literal: " Yizhaoxiong further impeached Magistrate Li Xianzhi for illegal levies burdening the people; because Xianzhi was also recommended by Fu, the emperor blamed Fu for deception and stripped his office;
translations.idiomatic: " Yizhaoxiong also impeached Magistrate Li Xianzhi for illegal exactions. Xianzhi too was Fu's choice; the emperor charged deceit and removed Fu from office;

sentences.zh: 下刑部、議政大臣等會鞫，紱罪凡二十一事，當斬。

translations.literal: the matter was sent to the Ministry of Punishments and princely councillors for joint trial; Fu's offenses totaled twenty-one items, warranting execution.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments and the princely council tried him on twenty-one counts calling for execution.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「紱既知悔過，情詞懇切，且其學問尚優，命免死，纂修八旗通志效力。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Since Fu knows repentance and his words are earnest, and his scholarship is still superior, his life is spared and he is ordered to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Eight Banners."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Fu shows repentance and his plea is earnest; his learning remains sound. Spare his life and set him to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Eight Banners."

sentences.zh: 七年，又以順承郡王錫保奏濟世在阿爾泰供言劾文鏡實受紱及珽指，下紱等刑部。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Prince Shuncheng Xibao further memorialized that at Altai Jishi had stated that impeaching Wenjing was really at the direction of Fu and Ting; Fu and the others were sent to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Prince Xibao reported that at Altai Jishi had testified the impeachment of Wenjing followed Fu's and Ting's orders; Fu was sent back to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 會曾靜、張熙獄起，上召王大臣宣諭，並命紱入，諭曰：「朕在籓邸，初不知珽、紱姓名。

translations.literal: When the cases of Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi arose the emperor summoned princes and ministers to announce the charges and also ordered Fu to enter; he instructed: "In my princely mansion I initially did not know Ting's and Fu's names."
translations.idiomatic: When the Zeng Jing and Zhang Xi affair broke, the emperor summoned princes and ministers, and Fu as well, and said: "In my days as heir I did not even know Ting's and Fu's names."

sentences.zh: 有馬爾濟哈者，能醫。

translations.literal: "There was one Ma'erjiha who could practice medicine."
translations.idiomatic: "A man named Ma'erjiha practiced medicine."

sentences.zh: 朕問：'更有能醫者否？

translations.literal: "I asked: 'Are there others who can practice medicine?'"
translations.idiomatic: "I asked whether anyone else could heal."

sentences.zh: '以珽對。

translations.literal: "'He named Ting in reply."
translations.idiomatic: "He mentioned Ting."

sentences.zh: 召珽來見，珽謂不當與諸王往來，辭不至，以是朕重之。

translations.literal: "I summoned Ting to an audience; Ting said he ought not associate with princes and declined to come; therefore I valued him."
translations.idiomatic: "I summoned Ting, but he refused to visit princes, so I esteemed him."

sentences.zh: 年羹堯來京，​​亟稱珽，朕告以嘗招之不來，羹堯以語珽，珽复辭不至，以是朕益重之。

translations.literal: "Nian Gengyao came to the capital and repeatedly praised Ting; I told him that I had once summoned Ting and he did not come; Gengyao told this to Ting, and Ting again declined to come; therefore I valued him all the more."
translations.idiomatic: "Gengyao came to court praising Ting. I told him Ting had once refused my summons; Gengyao relayed that, and Ting refused again—so my regard deepened."

sentences.zh: 及出為四川巡撫，詣熱河行在，始與相見，為朕言李紱。

translations.literal: "When he went out as governor of Sichuan he came to the Rehe traveling palace and first met me; he spoke to me of Li Fu."
translations.idiomatic: "As Sichuan governor he came to my traveling palace at Rehe and spoke of Li Fu—then I first heard of Fu."

sentences.zh: 朕知紱自此始。

translations.literal: "I knew of Fu from this point onward."
translations.idiomatic: "That was my first knowledge of Fu."

sentences.zh: 既即位，延訪人才，起紱原官。

translations.literal: "After I took the throne I sought out talent and restored Fu to his former office."
translations.idiomatic: "On my accession I sought talent and restored his former rank."

sentences.zh: 旋自侍郎出撫廣西，至為直隸總督，徇私廢公，沽名邀譽，致吏治廢弛，人心玩愒。

translations.literal: "Soon from vice minister he went out as Guangxi governor, up to Governor-General of Zhili, showing favoritism and neglecting public duty, currying reputation, causing administration to languish and minds to grow lax."
translations.idiomatic: "He rose from vice minister to Guangxi governor and eventually Zhili governor-general, yet showed favoritism, neglected duty, courted reputation, and let government and public spirit decay."

sentences.zh: 又如塞思黑自西大通調回，令暫住保定。

translations.literal: "Again, when Seshei was transferred back from Xidatong he was ordered to stay temporarily at Baoding."
translations.idiomatic: "When Seshei was moved back from Xidatong I had him wait at Baoding."

sentences.zh: 未幾，紱奏言遘病，不數​​日即死。

translations.literal: "Before long Fu memorialized that Seshei had fallen ill; within a few days he died."
translations.idiomatic: "Soon Fu reported illness; within days Seshei was dead."

sentences.zh: 奸黨遂謂朕授意於紱，使之戕害。

translations.literal: "Wicked partisans thereupon said I had instructed Fu to harm and kill him."
translations.idiomatic: "Malcontents then claimed I had ordered Fu to kill him."

sentences.zh: 今紱在此，試問朕嘗授意否乎？

translations.literal: "Now Fu is here—ask whether I ever gave such instruction."
translations.idiomatic: "Fu stands here—did I ever give such an order?"

sentences.zh: 塞思黑罪本無可赦，豈料其遽死？

translations.literal: "Seshei's crimes were in themselves unpardonable—who could have expected his sudden death?"
translations.idiomatic: "Seshei deserved death in any case—who expected him to die so soon?"

sentences.zh: 紱不將其病死明白於眾，致生疑議，紱能辭其過乎？

translations.literal: "Fu did not report clearly to the public that he died of illness, giving rise to suspicious talk—can Fu escape blame?"
translations.idiomatic: "Fu failed to announce plainly that illness killed him, inviting suspicion—can he deny fault?"

sentences.zh: 田文鏡公忠，而紱與珽極力陷害，使濟世誣劾，必欲遂其私怨。

translations.literal: "Tian Wenjing was loyal and public-spirited, yet Fu and Ting used all their strength to entrap him, making Jishi lodge false impeachment, determined to satisfy private resentment."
translations.idiomatic: "Wenjing served the state faithfully, yet Fu and Ting schemed against him and set Jishi on false charges to settle private grudges."

sentences.zh: 此風何可長也？

translations.literal: "How can such a practice be allowed to grow?"
translations.idiomatic: "How can such conduct be tolerated?"

sentences.zh: 」復下紱刑部嚴鞫，獄上，請治罪，上寬之。

translations.literal: " Again Fu was sent down to the Ministry of Punishments for strict interrogation; when the case was reported upward, punishment was requested, but the emperor was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu was again remanded to Punishments for rigorous questioning; the ministry sought conviction, but the emperor showed mercy.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，賜侍郎銜，管戶部三庫，尋授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, he was granted vice-ministerial rank, placed in charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon appointed vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong's accession he received vice-ministerial rank, oversaw Revenue's three treasuries, and soon became vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，方開博學鴻辭科，紱所舉已眾，又以所知囑副都御史孫國璽薦舉，事聞上，上詰紱，紱自承妄言，上謂「紱乃妄舉，非止妄言，避重就輕」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, as the Bozhong Hongci examination was opened, Fu's nominations were already numerous; he further had acquaintances he entrusted to Associate Censor-in-Chief Sun Guoxuan to recommend; when the matter reached the emperor, he questioned Fu; Fu admitted himself to reckless speech; the emperor said, "Fu made reckless nominations, not merely reckless speech—evading the serious and taking the light."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 1, when the erudite literary examination opened, Fu had already nominated many candidates and had Sun Guoxuan, associate censor, recommend more of his acquaintances. Summoned before the throne, Fu confessed to false statements. The emperor replied that reckless nomination, not mere words, was the offense—he was shifting blame from the grave to the trivial.

sentences.zh: 降授詹事。

translations.literal: He was demoted and appointed Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二年，以母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the second year he returned home on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 六年，補光祿寺卿，遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was restored as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and transferred to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was reappointed director of court banquets and promoted to grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 紱偉岸自喜。

translations.literal: Fu was imposing in stature and pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was tall and self-satisfied in manner.

sentences.zh: 其論學大指，謂硃子道問學，陸九淵尊德性，不可偏廢，上聞而韙之。

translations.literal: The main drift of his learning held that Zhu Xi emphasized the Way through inquiry and Lu Jiuyuan honored moral nature—neither could be abandoned in part; when the emperor heard this he approved it.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship he held that Zhu Xi's stress on inquiry and Lu Jiuyuan's honor of moral nature must stand together; the emperor heard and agreed.

sentences.zh: 八年，以病致仕，入辭，上問：「有欲所陳否？

translations.literal: In the eighth year, on retiring for illness, he came to take leave; the emperor asked: "Is there anything you wish to present?"
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he retired for illness and came to bid farewell; the emperor asked, "Do you wish to say anything?"

sentences.zh: 」紱以慎終如始對，賜詩獎及之。

translations.literal: " Fu answered with "finish as you began," and was rewarded with an imperial poem praising him.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered that one must end as one began; the emperor granted a poem in praise.

sentences.zh: 十五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen he died.

sentences.zh: 孫友棠，乾隆十年進士，自編修累遷至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandson You Tang, a jinshi of the tenth year of Qianlong, rose from compiler through successive promotions to vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson You Tang, jinshi in Qianlong 10, rose from compiler to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 新昌舉人王錫侯撰字貫，坐悖逆死。

translations.literal: Xinchang licentiate Wang Xi Hou compiled the Zi Guan and was put to death on a charge of treasonous defiance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi Hou of Xinchang, a licentiate who compiled the Zi Guan, was executed for sedition.

sentences.zh: 友棠有題詩，並奪官，賜三品卿銜。

translations.literal: You Tang had inscribed a poem on it; his office was also stripped, and he was granted the rank of third-grade chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: You Tang had written a poem on the work; he too lost office but received a third-grade chamberlain's rank.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 蔡珽，字若璞，漢軍正白旗人，雲貴總督毓榮子。

translations.literal: Cai Ting, style Ruopu, was a man of the Plain White Banner of the Hanjun; son of Yunnan-Guizhou Governor Yurong.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ting, styled Ruopu, belonged to the Plain White Han Banner and was son of Governor Yurong of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十六年進士，改庶吉士，散館授檢討。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi he became a jinshi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and after leaving the academy was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Kangxi 36, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and after leaving the academy became a reviser.

sentences.zh: 洊擢少詹事，進翰林院掌院學士，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became Junior Tutor, then advanced to Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and concurrently vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through junior tutor to chancellor of the Hanlin and concurrent vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時世宗在潛邸，聞其能醫，欲見之，珽謝不往。

translations.literal: At that time Shizong was in the princely mansion; hearing that he could practice medicine, he wished to see him, but Ting declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizong was still heir, he heard Ting could heal and wished to meet him; Ting refused.

sentences.zh: 六十年，四川巡撫年羹堯入覲，世​​宗命達意，仍堅辭。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year Sichuan Governor Nian Gengyao came to audience; Shizong ordered him to convey his intent, but Ting still firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixty Sichuan governor Nian Gengyao came to court; Shizong had him convey the invitation, but Ting still refused.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，羹堯授川陝總督，以珽代為四川巡撫，覲聖祖熱河行在，世宗方扈從，乃詣謁而去。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year Gengyao was appointed governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi; Ting was made Sichuan governor in his stead; he attended the Kangxi emperor at the Rehe traveling palace; Shizong was then in attendance; only then did he go to pay his respects and depart.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Nian became governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi and Ting replaced him as Sichuan governor. At audience with Kangxi at Rehe, with Shizong in attendance, Ting at last paid his respects and left.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，羹堯請川、陝開採鼓鑄，珽疏言四川不產鉛，開採非便，羹堯劾珽阻撓，下部議，當奪官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, Gengyao requested mining and coinage in Sichuan and Shaanxi; Ting memorialized that Sichuan produced no lead and that mining would be inconvenient; Gengyao impeached Ting for obstruction; the ministries deliberated and he should have been stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2, Nian sought to open mining and minting in Sichuan and Shaanxi. Ting argued Sichuan lacked lead and mining would not serve. Nian impeached him for obstruction; the ministries ruled he should lose office.

sentences.zh: 珽辱重慶知府蔣興仁，憤自殺，珽以病卒聞，羹堯劾之，上詰責再三，始自承。

translations.literal: Ting insulted Chongqing Prefect Jiang Xingren, who in anger killed himself; Ting reported it as death from illness; Gengyao impeached him; the emperor questioned and reproached him repeatedly before he confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Ting humiliated Chongqing prefect Jiang Xingren, who killed himself in rage. Ting reported a natural death. Nian impeached him; only after repeated imperial questioning did he confess.

sentences.zh: 下部議，擬斬，詔逮至京師，召入見，具言羹堯貪暴及所以抗拒羹堯狀，上諭曰：「珽罪應如律，然劾之者羹堯，人將謂朕以羹堯故殺珽，是羹堯得操威福柄也。

translations.literal: The ministries deliberated and proposed execution; an edict ordered him seized and brought to the capital; summoned to audience, he fully described Gengyao's greed and violence and how he had resisted Gengyao; the emperor instructed: "Ting's crime should follow the law, yet his accuser is Gengyao; people will say I kill Ting because of Gengyao—that would let Gengyao wield the handle of favor and punishment."
translations.idiomatic: The ministries proposed execution; he was summoned to the capital and received in audience. He detailed Nian's greed and his own resistance. The emperor said Ting deserved death by law, but since Nian had impeached him, killing Ting would look like favoring Nian with the power of life and death.

sentences.zh: 其免珽罪。

translations.literal: Let Ting's crime be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Spare Ting.

sentences.zh: 」特授左都御史，兼正白旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: " He was specially appointed Left Censor-in-Chief and concurrently commander of the Plain White Banner Hanjun.
translations.idiomatic: " He was specially made left censor-in-chief and commander of the Plain White Han Banner.

sentences.zh: 尋進兵部尚書，仍兼左都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Minister of War while still holding the left censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became minister of war while retaining the left censorate.

sentences.zh: 會羹堯得罪，直隸總督李維鈞隱其財產，上命珽偕內大臣馬爾賽往按，得實，奪維鈞官，以珽署總督。

translations.literal: When Gengyao fell from favor, Zhili Governor Li Weijun had concealed his property; the emperor ordered Ting together with inner minister Ma'ersai to investigate; the facts were established; Weijun was stripped of office and Ting was made acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian fell, Zhili governor Li Weijun had hidden his property. Ting and Inner Minister Ma'ersai were sent to investigate, proved the charge, removed Weijun, and left Ting acting governor.

sentences.zh: 直隸方被水，議蠲賑，復發帑修河間、靜海諸城，俾饑民就傭受食。

translations.literal: Zhili had just suffered flooding; relief and tax exemption were discussed; treasury funds were also issued to repair the cities of Hejian, Jinghai, and others, so that famine victims might take employment and receive food.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili had just been flooded. Besides tax relief, treasury funds repaired Hejian, Jinghai, and other cities so the hungry could work for food.

sentences.zh: 珽奏言省會米貴，令按察使浦文倬至天津運截留漕米二萬石，以萬石運保定平糶，留萬石賑經過諸地，上如所請，敕再運通倉米十萬石往天津，加賑一月。

translations.literal: Ting memorialized that in the provincial capital rice was dear; he ordered Surveillance Commissioner Pu Wenzhao to Tianjin to transport twenty thousand shi of intercepted tribute grain—ten thousand shi to be transported to Baoding for sale at fair price, ten thousand shi left to relieve the districts along the route; the emperor approved as requested and ordered another hundred thousand shi from the Tong granary sent to Tianjin, with relief extended one month.
translations.idiomatic: Ting reported dear rice at the capital and sent Pu Wenzhao to Tianjin for twenty thousand shi of diverted tribute grain—half to Baoding for fair sale, half for districts along the route. The emperor agreed and sent another hundred thousand shi from Tong, adding a month of relief.

sentences.zh: 珽奏：「請察地方官侵冒，懲胥役虛報，訪衿棍挾制，貧民戶給印券，每村給村名紙旗，以次給領。

translations.literal: Ting memorialized: "I request investigation of local officials' embezzlement, punishment of clerks' false reporting, inquiry into gentry bullies' coercion, issuing stamped vouchers to poor households, giving each village a paper flag with the village name, and distributing in order."
translations.idiomatic: Ting proposed rooting out official embezzlement and clerk fraud, curbing gentry bullies, issuing stamped vouchers to the poor, village name flags for each hamlet, and orderly distribution.

sentences.zh: 賑滿，續修城工，即以賑時所給印券交驗受傭。

translations.literal: When relief was finished, city works were to be continued, and the stamped vouchers given during relief were to be presented for verification when hiring labor.
translations.idiomatic: After relief ended, wall repairs would continue, with the relief vouchers checked when men were hired.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 調補吏部尚書，仍兼領兵部、都察院及都統事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel while still concurrently directing the ministries of War and Justice and the banner command.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to minister of personnel while still overseeing war, the censorate, and the banner command.

sentences.zh: 四年，以珽所領事多，先後解左都御史、都統、吏部尚書，專任兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because the duties Ting held were many, he was successively relieved of the left censorate, banner command, and ministry of personnel, and devoted himself solely to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year four his posts were thinned: he gave up the left censorate, banner command, and personnel ministry, keeping only war.

sentences.zh: 旋以在直隸時徇庇昌平營參將楊雲棟，坐奪官，上命降授奉天府尹。

translations.literal: Soon, for while in Zhili having shown favor to Changping garrison Colonel Yang Yundong, he was sentenced to loss of office; the emperor ordered him demoted to prefect of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was stripped for favoring Colonel Yang Yundong of the Changping garrison while in Zhili; the emperor demoted him to Fengtian prefect.

sentences.zh: 初，上以岳鍾琪代年羹堯為川陝總督，珽入對，言鍾琪叵測。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor replaced Nian Gengyao with Yue Zhongqi as governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi, Ting entered audience and said Zhongqi was unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yue Zhongqi replaced Nian as Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general, Ting told the throne that Yue was untrustworthy.

sentences.zh: 鍾琪入覲，過保定，珽方署直隸總督，造蜚語，冀以撼鍾琪。

translations.literal: When Zhongqi came to audience and passed Baoding, Ting was then acting Zhili governor; he fabricated slander, hoping thereby to shake Zhongqi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue came to court and passed Baoding, Ting as acting Zhili governor spread rumors to undermine him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上嚴旨詰責。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor issued a stern edict of reproach.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of it and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 五年，召回京按訊，上閱羹堯幕客舉人汪景祺所著書，載珽撫四川時得夔州府知府程如絲賄，保治行第一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled to the capital for investigation; the emperor read the book composed by licentiate Wang Jingqi, a client of Gengyao, which recorded that when Ting governed Sichuan he had received bribes from Kuizhou Prefect Cheng Rusi and ranked his administration first.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he was recalled for inquiry. The emperor read a book by Nian's client Wang Jingqi stating that as Sichuan governor Ting had taken bribes from Kuizhou prefect Cheng Rusi and ranked him first in conduct.

sentences.zh: 如絲守夔州，鬻私鹽，而捕湖廣民鬻私鹽者得輒殺之，為羹堯劾罷。

translations.literal: While Rusi held Kuizhou he sold private salt, yet whenever he captured Huguang people selling private salt he would kill them; Gengyao impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Rusi had sold private salt in Kuizhou while killing Huguang smugglers he caught; Nian had impeached and removed him.

sentences.zh: 珽入對，言其冤。

translations.literal: Ting entered audience and said he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Ting told the throne Rusi was innocent.

sentences.zh: 上命免如絲罪，且擢為四川按察使。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Rusi's crime remitted and even promoted him to Sichuan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned Rusi and promoted him to Sichuan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至是，上頗疑景祺言。

translations.literal: At this point the emperor came to doubt Jingqi's words somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had begun to doubt Wang Jingqi's account.

sentences.zh: 會巡撫馬會伯劾如絲營私網利疏至，命侍郎黃炳如四川按其事，以珽偕炳還奏，事實，下法司匯讞。

translations.literal: When Governor Ma Huibo impeached Rusi for private profiteering, the emperor ordered Vice Minister Huang Bing to investigate in Sichuan; Ting accompanied Bing and on return reported the facts; the case was sent to the judiciary for combined sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Ma Huibo impeached Rusi for profiteering, Vice Minister Huang Bing was sent to Sichuan with Ting; their report confirmed the charges and the case went to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 尋議珽挾詐懷私，受夔關稅銀、富順縣鹽規，冒銷庫帑，並得如絲銀六萬六千、金九百，讒毀鍾琪，交結查嗣庭，凡十八事，應斬決，妻子入辛者庫，財產沒入官，命改斬監候。

translations.literal: Soon it was decided that Ting had practiced deceit from private motive, received Kuizhou customs silver and Fushun county salt levies, falsely expended treasury funds, and moreover received from Rusi sixty-six thousand taels of silver and nine hundred taels of gold, slandered Zhongqi, and associated with Zha Siting—in all eighteen matters warranting execution; wife and children to the Sinier treasury, property confiscated; the order was changed to execution deferred.
translations.idiomatic: Ting was found guilty on eighteen counts—including fraud, Kuizhou customs silver, Fushun salt dues, treasury abuse, sixty-six thousand taels and nine hundred taels of gold from Rusi, slandering Yue, and ties to Zha Siting—warranting death; family to bondage and goods seized; the sentence became deferred execution.

sentences.zh: 六年，管理正白旗信郡王德昭又奏珽家藏硃批奏摺三件未繳進，大不敬，應立斬，詔逮至京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Prince Xin of the Plain White Banner, Dezhao, further memorialized that three vermilion-annotated memorials were found hidden in Ting's house and not submitted—great irreverence, warranting immediate execution; an edict ordered him seized to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year six Prince Dezhao reported three vermilion-annotated memorials hoarded in Ting's house—capital crime; he was ordered to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，珽故吏知縣黃振國坐事奪官，珽薦起河南信陽知州，巡撫田文鏡劾貪劣不法。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ting's former clerk Magistrate Huang Zhenguo had been stripped for an offense; Ting recommended his restoration as prefect of Xinyang in Henan; Governor Tian Wenjing impeached him as greedy, base, and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ting's clerk Huang Zhenguo had lost office; Ting had him made Xinyang prefect in Henan; Governor Tian Wenjing impeached him as corrupt and lawless.

sentences.zh: 李紱自廣西巡撫遷直隸總督，入對，力陳振國無罪，御史謝濟世劾文鏡亦及之，言與紱合。

translations.literal: Li Fu, transferred from Guangxi governor to Zhili governor, on entering audience strongly stated that Zhenguo was innocent; Censor Xie Jishi in impeaching Wenjing also touched on this, speaking in accord with Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, moved from Guangxi to Zhili governor, insisted at audience that Zhenguo was innocent; Censor Xie Jishi's impeachment of Wenjing agreed with Fu on this point.

sentences.zh: 上疑紱與濟世為黨，召紱還京師，戍濟世。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected Fu and Jishi were a faction; Fu was summoned back to the capital and Jishi was banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected a clique; he recalled Fu to the capital and sent Jishi to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 及珽至，諭暴珽等結黨欺罔、傾陷文鏡諸罪狀，命斬振國，珽仍改斬監候，下獄。

translations.literal: When Ting arrived, the emperor set forth at length the crimes of Ting and others in forming factions to deceive and entrap Wenjing; he ordered Zhenguo executed; Ting was again changed to deferred execution and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting arrived, the emperor denounced the faction's deceit and plots against Wenjing, executed Zhenguo, commuted Ting's death again, and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，高宗即位，赦免。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when Gaozong took the throne, he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen Gaozong's accession brought amnesty.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，卒

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qianlong 8.

sentences.zh: 謝濟世，字石霖，廣西全州人。

translations.literal: Xie Jishi, style Shilin, was a native of Quanzhou in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jishi, styled Shilin, came from Quanzhou in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十七年，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Kangxi he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 47 he ranked first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，成進士，改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he became a jinshi, was made a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifty-one he became jinshi, Hanlin bachelor, and reviser.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，考選浙江道御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was selected as censor of the Zhejiang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 he was made censor of the Zhejiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 未浹旬，疏劾河南巡撫田文鏡營私負國，貪虐不法，列舉十罪。

translations.literal: Before ten days had passed he memorialized impeaching Henan Governor Tian Wenjing for pursuing private gain against the state, greed and cruelty, and lawlessness, listing ten crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he impeached Henan governor Tian Wenjing for private gain against the state, greed, cruelty, and lawlessness in ten counts.

sentences.zh: 上方倚文鏡，意不懌，命還濟世奏，濟世堅持不可。

translations.literal: The emperor was then relying on Wenjing and was displeased; he ordered Jishi's memorial returned; Jishi firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relied on Wenjing and was displeased; he ordered the memorial withdrawn; Jishi refused.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「文鏡秉公持正，實心治事，為督撫中所罕見者，貪贓壞法，朕保其必無，而濟世於督撫中獨劾文鏡，朕不知其何心？

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "Wenjing is fair and upright, sincere in governing affairs—a rarity among governors—and I guarantee he is free of corruption and law-breaking; yet Jishi alone among governors impeaches Wenjing—what is his intent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said Wenjing was upright and sincere—a rare governor—and swore he was no grafter; yet Jishi alone impeached him—what did Jishi mean?

sentences.zh: 朕訓誡科道至再至三，誠以科道無私，方能彈劾人之有私者。

translations.literal: "I have admonished the censorate again and again, truly because only when censors are selfless can they impeach those who are selfish."
translations.idiomatic: "I have warned the censorate repeatedly: only the selfless can impeach the selfish."

sentences.zh: 若自恃為言官，聽人指使，顛倒是非，擾亂國政，為國法所不容。

translations.literal: "If one relies on being a remonstrating official, listens to others' direction, inverts right and wrong, and disturbs state affairs, that is what state law will not permit."
translations.idiomatic: "To play remonstrator at another's bidding, invert truth, and disturb government is forbidden by law."

sentences.zh: 朕豈不知誅戮諫官史書所戒？

translations.literal: "Do I not know that executing remonstrating officials is what histories warn against?"
translations.idiomatic: "Do I not know histories warn against killing remonstrators?"

sentences.zh: 然誅戮諫官之過小，釀成人心世道之害大。

translations.literal: "Yet the fault in executing remonstrating officials is small, while the harm brewed to human hearts and the age is great."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet the fault of killing one remonstrator is small beside the harm to hearts and the age."

sentences.zh: 禮義不愆，何卹於人言，朕豈卹此區區小節哉？

translations.literal: "When ritual and righteousness are not violated, why shrink from men's talk—would I shrink from this petty scruple?"
translations.idiomatic: "When ritual and righteousness stand firm, why fear gossip—should I fear this petty scruple?"

sentences.zh: 」奪濟世官，下大學士、九卿、科道會鞫，濟世辨甚力。

translations.literal: " Jishi's office was stripped; the Grand Secretaries, the Nine Ministers, and the censorate were ordered to interrogate jointly; Jishi argued with great force.
translations.idiomatic: " Jishi was dismissed; grand secretaries, nine ministers, and censors tried him; he argued fiercely.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書勵杜訥問：「指使何人？

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Li Dunuo asked: "Who directed you?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Punishments Li Dunuo asked, "Who directed you?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「孔、孟。

translations.literal: " He answered: "Confucius and Mencius."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Confucius and Mencius."

sentences.zh: 」問：「何故？

translations.literal: " He was asked: "For what reason?"
translations.idiomatic: " He was asked why.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「讀孔、孟書，當忠諫。

translations.literal: " He said: "Reading the books of Confucius and Mencius, one ought to remonstrate loyally."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Reading Confucius and Mencius, one must remonstrate loyally."

sentences.zh: 見姦弗擊，非忠也！

translations.literal: "To see wickedness and not strike at it is not loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: "To see evil and not strike is not loyalty!"

sentences.zh: 」讞上，以濟世所言風聞無據，顯係聽人指使，要結朋黨，擬斬。

translations.literal: " When the sentence was reported upward, because Jishi's words were hearsay without basis and clearly showed he listened to others' direction and sought factional ties, execution was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " The sentence held his charges were hearsay, clearly directed by others in faction; death was proposed.

sentences.zh: 文鏡劾屬吏黃振國、邵言綸、汪諴等，李紱訟言其枉，並謂河南諸吏張球最劣，文鏡縱弗糾。

translations.literal: Wenjing impeached subordinate officials Huang Zhenguo, Shao Yinlun, Wang Qian, and others; Fu pleaded that they had been wronged, and also said that among Henan officials Zhang Qiu was the worst yet Wenjing would not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing impeached Huang Zhenguo, Shao Yinlun, Wang Qian, and others; Fu pleaded their innocence and said Zhang Qiu was Henan's worst yet Wenjing would not touch him.

sentences.zh: 入對，具為上言之。

translations.literal: On entering audience he fully reported this to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Fu laid this out to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上先入文鏡言，不直紱，而濟世罪狀文鏡又及枉振國、言綸、諴庇球諸事。

translations.literal: The emperor had already been predisposed by Wenjing's words and did not side with Fu; yet Jishi's charges against Wenjing also touched on the wrongful cases of Zhenguo, Yinlun, and Qian and shielding Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already favored Wenjing's account over Fu's, while Jishi's charges also covered the wrongful cases and Wenjing's protection of Qiu.

sentences.zh: 上召大學士、九卿、科道等入見，舉前事，謂：「濟世言與紱奏一一吻合，今詰濟世劾文鏡諸事，濟世皆茫無憑據，俯首無詞，是其受人指使，情弊顯見。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the Grand Secretaries, Nine Ministers, censors, and others to audience, recited the earlier matters, and said: "Jishi's words match Fu's memorial point for point; now when Jishi is questioned on his impeachment of Wenjing, he has no basis for any of it and bows his head without words—clearly he was directed by others; the fraud is obvious."
translations.idiomatic: Summoning grand secretaries, ministers, and censors, the emperor said Jishi's words matched Fu's memorial exactly; questioned on each charge, Jishi had no evidence and was silent—proof of direction by others.

sentences.zh: 」命奪濟世官，往阿爾泰軍前效力贖罪。

translations.literal: " He ordered Jishi stripped of office and sent to the Altai army front to redeem guilt through service.
translations.idiomatic: " Jishi lost office and was sent to Altai to redeem guilt in service.

sentences.zh: 濟世至軍，大將軍平郡王福彭頗敬禮之，濟世講學著書不稍輟。

translations.literal: When Jishi reached the army, Generalissimo Prince Ping Fu Peng treated him with considerable respect; Jishi lectured on learning and wrote books without the slightest pause.
translations.idiomatic: At the front Generalissimo Prince Fu Peng treated him with respect; Jishi lectured and wrote without pause.

sentences.zh: 七年，振武將軍順承郡王錫保以濟世撰古本大學注毀謗程、硃，疏劾，請治罪。

translations.literal: In the seventh year General Zhenwu Prince Xibao, because Jishi had composed a commentary on the ancient text Great Learning slandering Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi, memorialized impeachment and requested punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Prince Xibao impeached Jishi for a commentary on the ancient Great Learning that slandered Cheng Yi and Zhu Xi and sought punishment.

sentences.zh: 上摘「見賢而不能舉」兩節注，有「拒諫飾非，拂人之性」語，責濟世怨望謗訕，下九卿、翰詹、科道議罪。

translations.literal: The emperor extracted the commentary on the two sections "seeing the worthy and being unable to raise him" with the words "rejecting remonstrance, covering faults, going against human nature"; he reproached Jishi for resentment and slander and sent the case to the Nine Ministers, Hanlin, and censors for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cited Jishi's note on "seeing the worthy yet unable to raise him," with words about rejecting remonstrance and masking faults, charged resentment and slander, and sent the case to ministers, Hanlin, and censors.

sentences.zh: 有陸生棻者，自舉人選授江南吳縣知縣，引見，上有所詰問，不能對，改授工部主事。

translations.literal: There was one Lu Shengfen who, from licentiate, was selected and appointed magistrate of Wu county in Jiangnan; at audience the emperor questioned him and he could not answer; he was changed to a clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shengfen, selected from licentiate to magistrate of Wu in Jiangnan, failed the emperor's questions at audience and was made a works clerk.

sentences.zh: 復引見，上見其傲慢，以其廣西人，疑與濟世為黨，命奪官發軍前，令與濟世同效力。

translations.literal: At a second audience the emperor saw his arrogance; because he was a Guangxi man, he suspected he was of Jishi's faction; he ordered his office stripped and sent to the army front, ordered to serve together with Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: At a second audience the emperor found him arrogant; as a Guangxi man he was suspected of Jishi's faction, stripped of office, and sent to serve with Jishi.

sentences.zh: 生棻撰通鑑論十七篇，錫保以為非議時政，別疏論劾。

translations.literal: Shengfen composed seventeen chapters of Discourses on the Comprehensive Mirror; Xibao held that they criticized current policy and separately memorialized impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfen wrote seventeen chapters of Discourses on the Comprehensive Mirror; Xibao deemed them attacks on policy and impeached separately.

sentences.zh: 上並下九卿、翰詹、科道議罪，尋議濟世詆訕怨望，怙惡不悛，生棻憤懣猖狂，悖逆恣肆，皆於軍前正法。

translations.literal: The emperor sent both to the Nine Ministers, Hanlin, and censors for sentencing; soon it was decided that Jishi had slandered from resentment and clung to evil without reform, while Shengfen was resentful, frantic, and recklessly defiant—in both cases execution at the army front was warranted.
translations.idiomatic: Both cases went to ministers, Hanlin, and censors; soon Jishi was judged slanderous and unreformed, Shengfen frantic and defiant—both to be executed at the front.

sentences.zh: 上密諭錫保誅生棻，縛濟世使視，生棻既就刑，宣旨釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly instructed Xibao to execute Shengfen, bound Jishi to watch; after Shengfen had been executed, an edict was proclaimed releasing Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly ordered Xibao to execute Shengfen, bound Jishi to watch, then proclaimed Jishi's release.

sentences.zh: 濟世在戍九年，高宗即位，詔開言路，為建勳將軍欽拜草奏，請責成科道嚴不言之罰，恕妄言之罪，上嘉納焉。

translations.literal: Jishi was on frontier service nine years; when Gaozong took the throne, edicts opened the way of speech; for Merit-building General Qin Bai he drafted a memorial requesting that censors be held to strict penalties for silence and pardoned for reckless speech; the emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years on the frontier, Gaozong opened remonstrance; Jishi drafted for General Qin Bai a memorial urging strict penalties for censorial silence and pardon for rash speech; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 旋召濟世還京師，复補江南道御史。

translations.literal: Soon Jishi was summoned back to the capital and restored as censor of the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled and restored as Jiangnan circuit censor.

sentences.zh: 濟世以所撰大學注、中庸疏進上，略言：「大學注中，九卿、科道所議諷刺三語，臣已改刪，惟分章釋義，遵古本不遵程、硃，習舉業者有成規，講道學者無厲禁。

translations.literal: Jishi presented his commentary on the Great Learning and subcommentary on the Doctrine of the Mean, briefly stating: "In the Great Learning commentary, the three phrases on which the Nine Ministers and censors deliberated as satire I have already revised and deleted; only in dividing chapters and explaining meaning do I follow the ancient text and not Cheng and Zhu—those studying for the examinations have fixed rules, while those lecturing on the Way have no stern prohibition."
translations.idiomatic: He presented his Great Learning commentary and Mean subcommentary, noting he had deleted the three satirical lines censured by ministers and censors, followed the ancient text not Cheng and Zhu in chapter division, and asked that examination rules not bar moral inquiry.

sentences.zh: 千慮一得，乞捨其瑕而取其瑜。

translations.literal: "From a thousand deliberations one gain—I beg to discard the flaws and take the excellence."
translations.idiomatic: "From a thousand plans one good point—I beg you discard flaws and keep merit."

sentences.zh: 」得旨嚴飭，還其書。

translations.literal: " He received a stern edict of reproof and his books were returned.
translations.idiomatic: " He received stern rebuke and his books were returned.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年，濟世疏曰：「臣今所言者有二：一曰去邪勿疑，一曰出令勿貳。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong Jishi memorialized: "What your servant speaks of today has two points: first, remove the wicked and do not doubt; second, issue orders and do not doubt twice."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 Jishi memorialized: "Your servant has two points: remove the wicked without doubt, and issue orders without second thoughts."

sentences.zh: 有罪而復用，如程元章、哈元生者，輿論猶有恕詞；

translations.literal: Those guilty yet restored to office, such as Cheng Yuanzhang and Ha Yuansheng, still find some forgiveness in public opinion;
translations.idiomatic: Men guilty yet re-employed, like Cheng Yuanzhang and Ha Yuansheng, still draw some public indulgence;

sentences.zh: 至於隆升，國人皆曰不可，猶未罷斥。

translations.literal: as for promotion, the whole realm says it cannot be done, yet they are still not dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: but when promotion is urged, all say no, yet they are not removed.

sentences.zh: 不惟不罷斥隆升而已，如王士俊以加賦為墾荒，肆毒中州，又請為田文鏡立賢良祠。

translations.literal: Not only are they not dismissed from promoted rank—Wang Shijun took increased levies for land reclamation and ravaged the central provinces, yet again requested a shrine to the worthy for Tian Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, Wang Shijun disguised tax hikes as reclamation, ravaged the central provinces, and still sought a shrine to Wenjing as a worthy.

sentences.zh: 皇上既深惡之，乃調回而仍用，逮勘而復赦，乃者清問及之，議者謂將用為籓臬。

translations.literal: Your Majesty already deeply detested this, yet he was transferred back and still employed; when investigated he was again pardoned; now at the imperial inquiry some say he will be used as governor or surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The throne already despised him, yet recalled and reused him; investigated, then pardoned; now some say he will be made governor or commissioner.

sentences.zh: 籓臬總一省刑名錢穀，豈辜恩負罪之督撫所能勝任乎？

translations.literal: Governors and commissioners oversee a province's punishments and revenue—can one who has betrayed favor and borne guilt fill such a post?
translations.idiomatic: Governors and commissioners hold a province's law and revenue—can a man who betrayed grace and bears guilt fill such posts?

sentences.zh: 易言渙汗，禮稱綸綍，信而已矣。

translations.literal: The Changes speak of sweat dispersing; the Rites call the edict the imperial cord—trust alone suffices.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes speak of sweat dispersing; the Rites call the edict the cord of command—trust alone matters.

sentences.zh: 今則元年諭旨，二年即廢格或改易矣；

translations.literal: Now edicts of the first year are in the second year abandoned or altered;
translations.idiomatic: Yet first-year edicts are abandoned or changed in the second;

sentences.zh: 特諭停止在任守制，近日督撫又漸次請行。

translations.literal: a special edict stopped mourning in office, yet recently governors and commissioners have again gradually requested permission to observe it.
translations.idiomatic: a special order ended mourning in office, yet governors again seek permission to observe it.

sentences.zh: 天下之大，何患無才？

translations.literal: Under Heaven's vastness, what fear is there of lacking talent?
translations.idiomatic: Under vast Heaven, is talent so scarce?

sentences.zh: 記曰'金革無闢'，又曰'君子不奪人之親'，安用此食祿忘親者為哉？

translations.literal: The Record says, 'In war and emergency there is no avoidance of mourning,' and again, 'The gentleman does not deprive others of their kin'—why employ these who draw salary yet forget their parents?
translations.idiomatic: The classics say that in war one may set mourning aside, and that a gentleman does not steal another's parent from him—what need is there for officials who take pay yet abandon their filial duty?

sentences.zh: 特諭監生准入場不准考職。

translations.literal: A special edict allowed purchased students to sit examinations but not to qualify for office through examination.
translations.idiomatic: A special order let purchased students take exams but barred them from the examination route to office.

sentences.zh: 昨世宗升祔恩詔，監生仍准考職。

translations.literal: Yesterday, in the amnesty edict for Shizong's enshrinement, purchased students were again allowed to qualify for office.
translations.idiomatic: Only yesterday, in the amnesty for Yongzheng's enshrinement, purchased students were again permitted to qualify for posts.

sentences.zh: 考職者入仕之門，既準捐監，又准考職，復開捐例之張本也。

translations.literal: Qualification for office is the gate to service; to allow purchase of student status and also qualification for office is to reopen the root of sale-of-office precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Examination qualification is the door to office; permitting both purchased status and qualification is to lay the groundwork for selling posts all over again.

sentences.zh: 即止給虛銜，不准實授，而後命前命相違，亦不宜如此。

translations.literal: Even if one stops at empty titles without actual appointment, later orders that contradict earlier ones are likewise improper.
translations.idiomatic: Even limiting grants to empty titles without real appointment still leaves later edicts contradicting earlier ones—such inconsistency should not stand.

sentences.zh: 臣聞不退不遠，大學所譏，世間君子少、小人多，已敗露者不行放流，未敗露者益無忌憚。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that without retreat there is no advance—a point the Great Learning ridicules; in the world gentlemen are few and petty men many; those already exposed are not banished, while those not yet exposed grow all the bolder.
translations.idiomatic: I recall the Great Learning's rebuke that without stepping back one cannot move forward. Gentlemen are scarce and small men plentiful; exposed wrongdoers are not removed, while the undetected grow reckless.

sentences.zh: 若發號施令，小人得以搖奪，君子無所適從，國事未有不隳者也。

translations.literal: If in issuing orders petty men may sway them and gentlemen have nowhere to turn, state affairs cannot but collapse.
translations.idiomatic: When petty men can twist every command and honest men no longer know which way to turn, the state cannot fail to unravel.

sentences.zh: 三年，疏言：「母蔣年七十一，行動艱難，耳目昏憒。

translations.literal: In the third year he memorialized: "My mother Jiang is seventy-one, her movements difficult and her hearing and sight dim."
translations.idiomatic: In year three he wrote: "My mother Jiang is seventy-one, barely able to walk and nearly deaf and blind."

sentences.zh: 臣欲歸養，則貧不能供甘旨；

translations.literal: "If your servant wishes to return and support her, poverty prevents providing delicacies;"
translations.idiomatic: "If I return to care for her, I am too poor to keep her properly;"

sentences.zh: 欲迎養，則老不能任舟車；

translations.literal: "if he wishes to bring her to him, she is too old to bear boat and carriage;"
translations.idiomatic: "if I bring her here, she cannot endure the journey;"

sentences.zh: 欲歸省，則往返動經半年。

translations.literal: "if he wishes to visit home, the round trip often takes half a year."
translations.idiomatic: "if I travel home, the round trip takes half a year."

sentences.zh: 在家不過數月，乍逢又別，既別難逢，慈母之涕淚轉添，遊子之方寸終亂。

translations.literal: "At home he can stay only a few months; they meet and part again; once parted, reunion is hard; the fond mother's tears increase, and the wanderer's heart is ever unsettled."
translations.idiomatic: "A few months at home, then parting again—reunion rare, my mother's tears ever fresh, my own mind never at peace."

sentences.zh: 臣才不稱道府，例又從無自請遷轉。

translations.literal: "Your servant's talent does not suit a circuit intendancy, and precedent never allows one to request transfer on one's own."
translations.idiomatic: "I am unfit for a circuit post, and custom never permits an officer to ask for transfer himself."

sentences.zh: 乞敕部以州縣降授湖南、廣東，量予近地，臣得母子聚首，無任哀懇。

translations.literal: "He begs the ministries to assign him a county or prefecture in Hunan or Guangdong at reduced rank, granting a place as near as possible, that mother and son may meet—your servant's plea is boundless."
translations.idiomatic: "I beg the ministries to appoint me to a county in Hunan or Guangdong, as near my home as may be, that my mother and I may be together—I plead with all my heart."

sentences.zh: 」上特授濟世湖南糧儲道。

translations.literal: " The emperor specially appointed Jishi Grain Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor specially made him Hunan grain commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年，濟世聞衡陽知縣李澎徵賦縱丁役索浮費，易服偽為鄉民納賦者以往，察得實，善化知縣樊德貽與同弊，濟世詳劾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Jishi heard that Hengyang Magistrate Li Peng in collecting taxes let clerks extort extra fees; he changed clothes and posed as a villager paying tax, found the facts true, and that Changhua Magistrate Fan Deyi shared the abuse; Jishi memorialized in full impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Jishi learned that Hengyang Magistrate Li Peng's tax collectors were extorting surcharges. Disguised as a taxpayer he confirmed it, found Changhua Magistrate Fan Deyi complicit, and impeached both in detail.

sentences.zh: 巡撫許容庇德貽等，以濟世盪檢逾閒列狀入告。

translations.literal: Governor Xu Rong shielded Deyi and the others, and memorialized that Jishi had violated propriety and overstepped bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xu Rong protected Deyi and reported that Jishi had breached decorum.

sentences.zh: 上命解任，交總督孫嘉淦會鞫，濟世捕衡陽丁役下長沙知府張琳，讞得徵收浮費有據。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jishi relieved and referred the case to Governor-General Sun Jiagan for joint trial; Jishi arrested Hengyang clerks and sent them to Changsha Prefect Zhang Lin; deliberation found proof of collecting extra fees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspended him and sent the case to Governor-General Sun Jiagan. Jishi arrested the Hengyang clerks and handed them to Changsha Prefect Zhang Lin; review proved the surcharges.

sentences.zh: 容令岳常澧道倉德代濟世，布政使張璨附容指，貽書倉德，令更易長沙府詳牒。

translations.literal: Rong had Yue-Chang-Li Circuit Intendant Cang De replace Jishi; Provincial Commissioner Zhang Can sided with Rong and wrote Cang De ordering him to alter the Changsha prefecture's detailed report.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had Circuit Intendant Cang De take Jishi's place; Provincial Commissioner Zhang Can backed Rong and wrote Cang De to change Changsha's official report.

sentences.zh: 倉德初官給事中，嘗劾濟世奏事失儀，至是不直璨所為，發其書上嘉淦及漕運總督顧琮，嘉淦庇容，寢其事。

translations.literal: Cang De had first served as supervising secretary and once impeached Jishi for impropriety at audience; now disapproving Can's conduct, he forwarded the letter to Jiagan and Grain Transport Governor Gu Cong; Jiagan shielded Rong and shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Cang De, once a supervising secretary who had impeached Jishi for a breach of court etiquette, now disapproved of Can's letter and sent it to Jiagan and Transport Governor Gu Cong. Jiagan protected Rong and buried the case.

sentences.zh: 諭倉德委曲善處，琮諮都察院奏聞。

translations.literal: He instructed Cang De to handle the matter tactfully; Gu consulted the Censorate to memorialize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The court told Cang De to settle matters discreetly; Gu asked the Censorate to report upward.

sentences.zh: 御史胡定糾容挾私誣劾，採湖南民謠，斥容與璨等朋謀傾濟世。

translations.literal: Censor Hu Ding impeached Rong for private motives in false accusation, citing Hunan folk songs, and charged Rong and Can with plotting to ruin Jishi.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hu Ding accused Rong of a biased false charge, citing Hunan street rhymes, and said Rong and Can had conspired against Jishi.

sentences.zh: 上命侍郎阿里袞如湖南會嘉淦按治，而倉德以嘉淦寢其事，复揭都察院奏聞。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Aligun to Hunan to join Jiagan in investigation; Cang De, because Jiagan had shelved the affair, again reported through the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Aligun to Hunan with Jiagan; when Jiagan suppressed the case, Cang De appealed again through the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 上責嘉淦草率扶同，召還京師，解容、璨任，奪琳、德貽、澎官。

translations.literal: The emperor blamed Jiagan for careless collusion, recalled him to the capital, removed Rong and Can from office, and stripped Lin, Deyi, and Peng of rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Jiagan for careless collusion, recalled him, dismissed Rong and Can, and deprived Lin, Deyi, and Peng of their posts.

sentences.zh: 阿里袞尋奏濟世被誣劾，請復官，容、璨及按察使王玠皆坐奪官，上命並罷嘉淦，而獎倉德及定，調濟世驛鹽道。

translations.literal: Aligun soon memorialized that Jishi had been falsely impeached and asked restoration; Rong, Can, and Surveillance Commissioner Wang Qi all lost office; the emperor also dismissed Jiagan, rewarded Cang De and Ding, and transferred Jishi to the courier-salt circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Aligun reported that Jishi had been framed and asked his reinstatement. Rong, Can, and Surveillance Commissioner Wang Qi were all removed; Jiagan was dismissed as well; Cang De and Ding were praised; Jishi was made courier-salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蔣溥代為巡撫，嗛濟世密進所著書，斥為離經畔道，上曰：「朕不以語言文字罪人。

translations.literal: Jiang Pu replaced him as governor, resented Jishi's secretly submitting his writings, and denounced them as heterodox; the emperor said: "I do not punish men for words and texts."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Pu became governor, disliked Jishi's private submissions, and called them heterodox. The emperor said, "I do not punish people for what they write."

sentences.zh: 」置不問。

translations.literal: " He let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: " He took no action.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復言其老病，乃命休致。

translations.literal: Before long he again reported Jishi's age and illness, and ordered retirement.
