translations.idiomatic: Soon he cited Jishi's age and illness again, and the emperor ordered him to retire.

sentences.zh: 歸家居十二年，卒，年六十有八。

translations.literal: He lived at home twelve years and died at sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement twelve years and died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 陳學海，字志澄，江西永豐人。

translations.literal: Chen Xuehai, styled Zhicheng, was a native of Yongfeng in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xuehai, whose style was Zhicheng, came from Yongfeng in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifty-second year of Kangxi, made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Kangxi 52 and entered the Hanlin as a bachelor.

sentences.zh: 與濟世友，授山東恩縣知縣，行取刑部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Friend of Jishi; appointed magistrate of En County in Shandong; selected as a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: A friend of Jishi's, he served as magistrate of En County, Shandong, was selected for Punishments, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 文鏡劾振國等，上遣侍郎海壽、史貽直往按，請以學海從，得文鏡欺罔狀，將以實入告，繼乃反之，學海爭不得。

translations.literal: When Wenjing impeached Zhenguo and others the emperor sent Vice Ministers Hai Shou and Shi Yizhi to investigate and asked that Xuehai accompany them; they obtained proof of Wenjing's deception and were about to report the facts, but then reversed themselves; Xuehai could not prevail in argument.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjing impeached Zhenguo and others, the emperor sent Vice Ministers Hai Shou and Shi Yizhi to investigate with Xuehai. They found Wenjing's deceit and meant to report it, then reversed their findings; Xuehai could not change their minds.

sentences.zh: 使還，擢御史，嘗以語濟世，濟世用是劾文鏡。

translations.literal: On return from the mission he was promoted to censor; he once told Jishi, and Jishi used this to impeach Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Back from the mission he became a censor and told Jishi what had happened; Jishi used it to impeach Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 既譴，學海不自安，次年，以病告。

translations.literal: After the reprimand Xuehai was ill at ease; the next year he reported illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the punishment Xuehai felt uneasy and the next year pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 都察院劾偽病，並及與濟世交關狀，奪官，命與濟世同效力軍前。

translations.literal: The Censorate impeached feigned illness and also his ties with Jishi; he was stripped of office and ordered to serve with Jishi before the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate charged sham illness and his connection with Jishi, removed his rank, and sent him to the frontier with Jishi.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，召還，授檢討。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng he was recalled and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 7 he was recalled and made a reviser.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year eleven.

sentences.zh: 論曰：田文鏡與鄂爾泰、李衛同為世宗所激賞。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tian Wenjing, along with Ortai and Li Wei, were alike highly commended by Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Tian Wenjing, like Ortai and Li Wei, won Yongzheng's highest praise.

sentences.zh: 高宗謂三人者文鏡為​​最下，允哉！

translations.literal: Gaozong said that of the three Wenjing was the lowest—indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong judged Wenjing the least of the three—rightly so!

sentences.zh: 文鏡馭屬吏苛急，待士尤虐。

translations.literal: Wenjing governed subordinates with harsh urgency and treated scholars with especial cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing drove his staff relentlessly and treated the literati with special harshness.

sentences.zh: 紱固以好士得時譽，宜其惡之深，而所爭以為枉者，為珽所薦吏。

translations.literal: Fu had indeed won contemporary reputation for loving scholars; it is fitting that Wenjing hated him deeply; yet those he claimed were wronged were clerks recommended by Ting.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's reputation rested on patronizing scholars, so Wenjing's hatred was natural—yet the men Fu defended were Ting's appointees.

sentences.zh: 濟世又繼以為言，世宗疑珽使紱入告，不納；

translations.literal: Jishi again took up the same argument; Shizong suspected Ting had sent Fu to report and did not accept it;
translations.idiomatic: Jishi repeated the charge; Yongzheng suspected Ting had put Fu up to it and would not listen;

sentences.zh: 又嗾濟世露章論劾，互相結，務欲傾文鏡。

translations.literal: then incited Jishi to open memorial impeachment—they banded together, determined to overthrow Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: then set Jishi to impeach Wenjing openly—they formed a faction bent on ruining him.

sentences.zh: 獄遂不可解，然終未即誅死。

translations.literal: The cases thus became insoluble, yet in the end they were not immediately executed.
translations.idiomatic: The trials tangled beyond unraveling, yet none were put to death at once.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣服，諸人皆得湔祓，紱復起，濟世亦見用。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded, all were able to wash away stain; Fu was restored, and Jishi also found employment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong all were rehabilitated—Fu returned to office and Jishi served again.

sentences.zh: 孰謂世宗嚴？

translations.literal: Who says Shizong was severe?
translations.idiomatic: Who calls Yongzheng harsh?

sentences.zh: 不肯戮諫臣，固明言之矣。

translations.literal: His refusal to slay remonstrating officials he stated plainly enough.
translations.idiomatic: He said plainly enough that he would not kill men who remonstrated.
